Rashi on Keritot 18b:12:1.english: [If] one ate and drank in one lapse of awareness - On Yom Kippur.

Rashi on Keritot 18b:12:2.english: He is liable [to bring] only one - For drinking is included in [the category of] eating.

Rashi on Keritot 18b:1:1.hebrew: ר' אליעזר היא - הילכך, ליכא למימר חולין לעזרה נינהו:
Rashi on Keritot 18b:1:1.english: It is Rabbi Eliezer - Therefore, one cannot say [that] they are unconsecrated [animals brought] into the Temple courtyard.

Rashi on Keritot 18b:1:2.hebrew: ואתני אי ראשון שומן אכל - ודאי השני חלב. ואי אכל ודאי חלב מספקא, ליהוי ליה כפרה להגין עליו עד שיודע לו ויביא חטאת; ואי לא, ליהוי נדבה:
Rashi on Keritot 18b:1:2.english: And stipulate: If the first [person] ate permitted fat - [then] certainly the second [ate] forbidden fat. And if he indeed ate forbidden fat in doubt, let it be an atonement for him to protect him until it becomes known to him and he brings a sin offering; and if not, let it be a gift [offering].

Rashi on Keritot 18b:2:1.english: And it became known to him - That it is uncertain.

Rashi on Keritot 18b:2:2.hebrew: כשם - שאם יודע לו באחרונה שכולן ודאי חלב היו, ודאי ליהוי מביא חטאת על כל אחת ואחת, דידיעות ספק שבינתים מחלקות לחטאות, דלא הוי העלם אחת:
Rashi on Keritot 18b:2:2.english: Just as - For if it becomes known to him in the end that all of them were definitely forbidden fat, he would certainly bring a sin offering for each and every one, since the intermediate [instances of] awareness of uncertainty separate [them] for sin offerings, as it is not a single lapse of awareness.

Rashi on Keritot 18b:2:3.english: So too, he brings a provisional guilt offering for each one - As long as definite knowledge has not become known to him.

Rashi on Keritot 18b:4:1.english: Here Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] taught - As I explained.

Rashi on Keritot 18b:8:1.english: If that is so, [someone] ate an olive-bulk of [forbidden] fat before Yom Kippur and an olive-bulk of [forbidden] fat after Yom Kippur - And both of them [were eaten] in one lapse of awareness.

Rashi on Keritot 18b:8:2.hebrew: במקום אשם תלוי - כדקתני בפ' בתרא (לקמן כריתות כה.): חייבי אשמות תלויים שעבר עליהן יום הכיפורים א' פטורין, והוה ליה כידיעת ספק:
Rashi on Keritot 18b:8:2.english: In place of a provisional guilt offering - As it is taught in the last chapter (below, Keritot 25a): Those liable for provisional guilt offerings over whom Yom Kippur has passed [are exempt], and [thus] it is like knowledge of uncertainty.

Rashi on Keritot 18b:9:1.hebrew: דילמא - הא דאמרינן יום הכיפורים מכפר, והוא דמתיידע ליה שספק חלב אכל:
Rashi on Keritot 18b:9:1.english: Perhaps - that which we say [that] Yom Kippur atones [is only] when it is known to him that he ate a doubtful [piece of] forbidden fat.

Rashi on Keritot 18b:9:2.hebrew: הודע ולא הודע תנן - בפ"ק דשבועות (דף יב:) מפרש בגמרא: בין שנודע לו ספקו, בין שלא נודע לו ספקו קודם יום הכיפורים — יוה"כ מכפר. אלמא, אף על גב דלא מתיידע ליה לגמרי, מכפר:
Rashi on Keritot 18b:9:2.english: We learned: [whether] he became aware or did not become aware - In the first chapter of Shevuot (12b), the Gemara explains: whether his doubt became known to him or whether his doubt did not become known to him before Yom Kippur, Yom Kippur atones. Thus, even though it was not completely known to him, it atones.

Tosafot on Keritot 18b:10:1.hebrew: הא דנקט חלב שחרית ביום הכיפורים - ולא נקט מילתא דהיתר וחייב קרבן עבור יום הכיפורים עצמו דאסורה באכילה, דאם כן צריך למינקט ככותבת, שהוא שיעור אכילת יום הכיפורים; ונקט שיעור זוטא, ולכך נקט כזית חלב שהוא פחות:
Tosafot on Keritot 18b:10:1.english: [The reason] that [the Gemara] mentions "forbidden fat on the morning of Yom Kippur" - and does not mention a permitted item [for which] one would be liable for an offering on account of Yom Kippur itself, since it is forbidden to eat [on Yom Kippur], [is] because if so, it would need to mention a date-bulk, which is the [minimum] measure for eating on Yom Kippur; and it [wanted to] mention a smaller measure, and therefore it mentioned an olive-bulk of forbidden fat, which is less.

Tosafot on Keritot 18b:7:1.hebrew: והתניא כל שחלוקות כו' - ואף על גב דר' יהודה קאמר לה לעיל (כריתות דף טו:), מכל מקום לא משמע דפליג עליה רבי בהא. לרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, הכי פירושו: כל שחלוקות לחטאות — כגון חלב ודם, פיגול ונותר — חלוקין לאשמות, דצריך להביא אשם תלוי על כל אחת ואחת; אבל בידיעה לא קמיירי. וגם לרבא, הכי פירושו: כל שחלוקות לחטאות בידיעת ודאי, חלוקות לאשמות בידיעת ספק:
Tosafot on Keritot 18b:7:1.english: "Isn't it taught [in a baraita]: Whatever are divided, etc." - And even though Rabbi Yehuda stated it above (Keritot 15b), nevertheless it does not seem that Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] disagrees with him on this. According to Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, this is its explanation: Whatever [transgressions] are divided for sin offerings—such as forbidden fat and blood, piggul, and notar—are divided for guilt offerings, so that one must bring a provisional guilt offering for each and every one; however, [the baraita] is not speaking about awareness. And also according to Rava, this is its explanation: Whatever [transgressions] are divided for sin offerings through definite awareness are divided for guilt offerings through uncertain awareness.

Tosafot on Keritot 18b:8:1.hebrew: אלא מעתה אכל כזית חלב לפני יוה"כ וכזית לאחר יוה"כ - דהשתא איכא שתי אשמות: אכילת חלב דלפני יוה"כ — כיפר יוה"כ במקום אשם, ואכילת חלב דלאחר יוה"כ — הביא עליו אשם; והשתא איכא ב' אשמות. הכי נמי, דאם נודע לו אחר כך על שניהן שיביא שתי חטאות? והא אכלם בהעלם אחת! אלא לא מייתי. ואם כן, שמע מינה דהאי כללא "כל שחלוקין כו'" ליתא, שהרי הכא איכא ב' אשמות וליכא כי אם חטאת אחת:
Tosafot on Keritot 18b:8:1.english: If that is so, [someone] ate an olive-bulk of [forbidden] fat before Yom Kippur and an olive-bulk after Yom Kippur - For now there are two guilt offerings: [for] the eating of [forbidden] fat before Yom Kippur, Yom Kippur atoned in place of a guilt offering, and [for] the eating of [forbidden] fat after Yom Kippur, he brought a guilt offering for it; and now there are two guilt offerings. [Would you say] so too, that if it became known to him afterward concerning both of them, he should bring two sin offerings? But he ate them in a single lapse of awareness! Rather, he does not bring [two sin offerings]. And if so, learn from this that this principle, "Whatever is divided, etc.," is not [valid], for behold, here there are two guilt offerings, yet there is only one sin offering.

Tosafot on Keritot 18b:9:1.hebrew: אמר ליה דילמא יום הכיפורים אינו מכפר אלא אם כן הודע - ועתה יש שתי חטאות כמו שתי אשמות. "אמר ליה רבא בר רב חנן תרדא" — רבא בר רב חנן היה חבר אביי, כדאיתא פרק כיצד מברכין (ברכות דף מו):
Tosafot on Keritot 18b:9:1.english: [Abaye] said to him: Perhaps Yom Kippur only atones if he became aware [of it] - And now there are two sin offerings, like two guilt offerings. "Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to him: Fool!" — Rava bar Rav Ḥanan was a colleague of Abaye, as is found in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Mevarekhin (Berakhot 46a).
